games.title: over the hill
games.description: Explore the world in the golden age of offroading. Drive iconic 4x4 vehicles from the 60s to 80s by yourself or with friends through challenging trails and beautiful scenery.

games.title: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2
games.description: Obliterate heretics in the name of the Emperor in Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2! Play as Ultramarine Malum Caedo or Sister of Battle Nyra Veyrath in this sequel to retro FPS Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun with MORE enemies, MORE weapons, and NEW ways to purge!

games.title: Planet Zoo 2
games.description:
Build a wilder world in Planet Zoo 2 – the sequel to the beloved zoo simulation game. Let your creativity soar by constructing and managing distinctive zoos around the world, full of awe-inspiring animals, including fully aquatic and flying species for the first time. Plus, take the next step in animal conservation and release your species into customisable, expansive Wildlife Reserves. 

AWE-INSPIRING ANIMALS 
Discover a diverse roster of animal species, each with their own needs & behaviours. New faces join familiar favourites like the African Lion and Western Chimpanzee to create iconic zoo rosters in jaw-dropping detail. 

Construct beautiful habitats for your animals to thrive in as they interact with the world around them in authentic ways. From authentic herding behaviours to grazing on the vegetation you provide for them. Experience a generational leap of animal detail and immersion with incredible natural movements and expressive emotions that bring each animal to life like never before. 

AWESOME AQUATICS 
Prepare your diving suit! Fully aquatic species make a splash in their stunning debut! Build custom spectacular freshwater or saltwater aquariums to home an exciting line-up of delightful swimming animals. A new world beneath the water awaits, filled with colourful shoals of fish, Black-tipped Reef Sharks, Hawksbill Turtles and so many more! 

FREQUENT FLYERS 
Soar to great heights with a diverse mix of bright & brilliant fully flying birds including the vibrant Toco Toucan and majestic Secretary Bird. House your birds in fully customisable aviaries built from barriers, support poles and dynamic mesh covers, allowing them to fly freely and safely. Observe their dynamic behaviours on the ground and in the sky as they glide around unique habitats. 

WILDLIFE RESERVES 
Conservation goes beyond your zoo! Take on global conservation projects and meet specific requirements to release your animals into fully customisable, expansive Wildlife Reserves across the globe in living ecosystems created by you.  

LET YOUR CREATIVITY SOAR 
Build the zoo of your dreams across multiple globe-spanning biomes, with four brand-new scenery themes covering iconic architecture from around the world and five returning themes from the original Planet Zoo, providing you with an expansive library of scenery items to build/create with. 

Effortlessly design your zoos using a range of ready-to-place blueprints or get creative with the Planet franchise’s iconic piece-by-piece construction tools to bring your own ideas to life. 

Delve into every detail with scaling, flexi-colour & easy-to-use pathing systems, together with new foliage and terrain brushes to make grand changes to your zoos and Wildlife Reserves. 

MEANINGFUL MANAGEMENT 
Construct perfect habitats for appealing animals to bring in guests, boosting your zoo’s rating and earning money to fund further expansion. 

Manage day-to-day zoo life as you create immersive spaces for your guests packed with educational opportunities around every corner. Cater to their requirements with a variety of shops and amenities to curate the perfect day out. 

A WILDER WORLD AWAITS 
Join FEN (Fauna and Ecosystems Network) in a fun-filled adventure around the world in Career mode. Build a global network of zoos and Wildlife Reserves and trade animals with other players in Franchise mode or enjoy unlimited creativity in Sandbox mode. 

CONNECTED COMMUNITY 
Discover a world of community content in the Frontier Workshop. Freely explore and download player-created blueprints and creations from across platforms and subscribe to your favourites to place them in your zoos.

games.title: Total War: SHOGUN 2 Complete Edition
games.description:
Experience the updated, enhanced, and complete version of the grand strategy classic; Total War: SHOGUN 2 and all of its DLC, including the Rise of the Samurai and Fall of the Samurai campaigns.

Wage total war, unite Japan and become Shogun. Master Bushido and Chi, war and peace, build alliances, lead massive armies, construct mighty castles and execute acts of cunning subterfuge to fuel your campaigns across the entire Shogun era from the rise of the first Shogun to the fall of the last Samurai.

Command massed armies of samurai warriors in dramatic real-time tactical battles. Master the tactics of the Shogun era and sweep across the battlefields of Feudal Japan, commanding massive, pitched battles, besieging towering fortresses, and springing devastating ambushes. Glorious victory or shameful defeat will be yours.

games.title: Valor Mortis
games.description:
You served Napoleon. You died for Napoleon. You have risen for Napoleon.

You are William, a soldier of the Grande Armée brought back from a battlefield grave. But the Europe you awaken to is not the one you sacrificed for. A mysterious plague now sweeps the continent, and you have been reborn with its corrupting power pulsing through your veins.

Valor Mortis is a first-person action soulslike from the creators of Ghostrunner. Rise from death as a former soldier of Napoleon’s army. Wield supernatural powers, battle horrifying monsters, and unravel a conspiracy that threatens all of humanity.

games.title: Allogloom
games.description: Join Nora in this mysterious and macabre point and click adventure game. Find and collect items to solve puzzles. Talk to peculiar people and monsters alike. Explore Gruesome Grove and beyond to uncover forgotten truths and save the people of her town!

games.title: Truckful
games.description:
Truckful is a single player car delivery adventure game based around completing errands and quests for villagers and uncovering the ancient mystery that surrounds the nearby old forest.

Drive your pickup truck through winding countryside roads, dusty lowlands and small towns. Upgrade the truck, improve its weight and load capacity to make it go faster through all kinds of demanding routes. Pack the bed with fragile & shaky cargo of all shapes and kinds, whether its ice cold fish that needs to be delivered fast, or a classic grandma vase that will put your driving skills to the true test.

The ancient forest on the countryside outskirts is unwelcoming to visitors and often mentioned in local legends and myths. The overwhelming feeling of something lurking in the tree branch shadows is hard to shake off. Face the adversity and uncover its deep roots.

games.title: Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen
games.description:
Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen enriches the dynamic fantasy world and expansive adventures of Dragon's Dogma 2 with unforgettable new tales and thrilling encounters.
    Based on feedback we received after the initial release of Dragon's Dogma 2, we established three goals for ourselves when we set out to update and expand the game:
    Enhanced gameplay. Expanded adventures. Enticing value.

games.title: Kingdom Hearts Collection I ~ III
games.description: A value‑packed bundle featuring three collections: KINGDOM HEARTS -HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX-, KINGDOM HEARTS HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue, and KINGDOM HEARTS III + Re Mind (DLC).

games.title: Echo Weaver
games.description:
Echo Weaver is a time loop metroidBRAINia where time is your best resource and secrets are your only upgrades. 

You're the last of the Weavers, a remnant of a ruined society trapped in a glitching time loop. The Congregation set out to explore the stars and find paradise. What they found instead has led their utopian project to ash and cinders.

Can you master time itself to unravel the conspiracy at the heart of Provenance?

games.title: Neon Abyss 2
games.description:
Dive deeper into the chaotic, beautifully pixelated Abyss with Neon Abyss 2! The action is faster, the stakes are higher, and the possibilities are endless in this cybermyth roguelike.

With explosive run 'n' gun gameplay, diverse combat styles, and unlimited item synergies, Neon Abyss 2 delivers a dramatic, thrill-packed experience every time you enter.

games.title: Order of the Sinking Star
games.description:
From legendary director Jonathan Blow (Braid, The Witness) comes Order of the Sinking Star, a massive narrative adventure featuring more than one thousand hand-crafted puzzles designed to put your intellect to the test. 

As Queen Effia, you are transported to a realm of curious magic, dangerous contraptions, and vicious monsters. As you make your way, you will explore four distinct worlds, each with its own mechanics, characters, and stories, and then watch as they all collide.

As the worlds merge, and characters meet one another, puzzle systems intertwine, creating surprising new gameplay possibilities. Explore at your own pace, revisit worlds and return to challenges as you see fit. Discover unique playable characters, master evolving gameplay mechanics, and decipher the deep mysteries of a sprawling, interconnected game world. 

Blending exploration, storytelling, and ever-progressing mechanics, Order of the Sinking Star invites you into a mysterious, living puzzle unlike anything you've played.

games.title: Silver Pines
games.description:
Private investigator Red Walker finds himself in Silver Pines, a place half-abandoned, half-forgotten, in the middle of nowhere on a job to track down Eddie Velvet. A musician who has vanished. As the case begins to reveal a dark past, Walker soon slips into a strange and nightmarish descent beyond his control.

Silver Pines is a survival horror metroidvania set in small town America. Fight nightmarish terrors and solve puzzles, while carefully managing your scarce resources as you uncover the mysteries that could hold the key to redemption.

games.title: Forever Ago
games.description:
Following a tragic stroke of fate, Alfred embarks on a journey north in search of redemption. In this single-player road trip adventure, you'll travel to beautiful places, capture memories with your camera, meet interesting characters, and even make some new friends.

Experience a nuanced and heartfelt story about broken dreams, loss, and regret - but also courage, hope, and true friendship. Learn about the stories, beliefs and struggles of characters you meet along the way, brought to life by renowned voice actors.

Explore beautiful environments, ranging from serene forest trails to dusty barrens sweltering in the desert sun. Examine and interact with objects to learn about your surroundings and the people living there. 

Play through a lifetime of love as Alfred with your sweetheart Audrey, experiencing a true love that transcends time.

games.title: Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival
games.description:
Experience a new chapter in the legendary horror series like never before. Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival takes first-person action horror survival to the next level.

Play the story of Aidan, who must use the power of a mysterious puzzle box – the Genesis Configuration – to help his girlfriend Sunny's escape from the otherworldly hellscape of the Labyrinth.

Wield the powers of the box to survive your bargain with the infamous Pinhead and do battle with the horrific cult devoted to the Cenobites.

A New Story in Hellraiser's Canon – Unwittingly kickstart Pinhead’s ritual to unleash greater pain and pleasure than ever before.

Harness the Power of the Box – Combine the unique, hellish abilities of the Configuration with an arsenal of earthly weapons to inflict bone-breaking, flesh-searing pain - or is it pleasure? - upon masochistic enemies.

Fight Against Unholy Enemies – Take on hell's wretches, deviants, cultists, and even its most infernal priests in a story-driven horror survival game.

games.title: Gears of War: E-Day
games.description:
Experience the brutal horror of Emergence Day through the eyes of Marcus Fenix in the origin story of one of gaming's most acclaimed sagas.​ 

Fourteen years before Gears of War, war heroes Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago return home to face a new nightmare: the Locust Horde. These subterranean monsters, grotesque and relentless, erupt from below, laying siege on humanity itself. ​

Built from the ground up with Unreal Engine 5, Gears of War: E-Day delivers unprecedented graphical fidelity.

games.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer
games.description:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a runs-based, high-stakes reinvention of racing born in the lawless Outer Rim of the Star Wars galaxy.  

The Empire’s grip on the galaxy has finally broken, and with its fall comes a new obsession: speed. As the New Republic struggles to rebuild, gambling, entertainment, and glory fuel a booming underground.  

Out of this chaos, The Galactic League is born: an unsanctioned racing circuit where syndicates sponsor pilots, fortunes are won and lost in seconds, and only the bold survive. 

No Force. No prophecy. Just skill, strategy, and the will to rise.

games.title: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve
games.description:
Step into the cockpit and take flight as an elite pilot across stunning skies. Enter intense dogfights, eliminate threats, and rise through gripping missions to earn your wings.

Campaign Mode showcases stunning visuals with dynamic multi-layered cloudscapes that capture the majesty of living skies. Feel the rush of a fast-paced arcade-style gameplay and deploy powerful weapons to dominate the battlefield.

Beyond the chaos in the air, breathtaking first-person scenes reveal your pilot’s story through breathtaking cinematics. Experience the pressure of command, the weight of decisions, and the bonds forged in battle. Between missions, bond with your squad members, rise to meet adversity, and prove yourself as a true ace.

games.title: Retrospace
games.description: Immersive, disco-punk, space horror where you can be a sneaky chap or a mutant action hero as you try to survive on a space station swallowed by a black hole. A mind-bending ride with weird creatures, immersive features, time jumps, and '70s mustaches!

games.title: Dynasty Warriors 3 Complete Edition Remastered
games.description: Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered is a striking modern revival of Dynasty Warriors 3 and Dynasty Warriors 3: Xtreme Legends, which established the foundation of the entire series for decades to come. Dynasty Warriors 3 was the first game in the Dynasty Warriors series to feature mechanics that would become a mainstay for the series, such as True Musou Attacks, two-player simultaneous play, and the officer development system. It was also the first game in the series to sell more than one million copies. While reproducing the movements of the original game, the action system of Dynasty Warriors 3 has evolved to be more brilliant and exhilarating. In Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered, players can experience 1 vs. 1,000 action woven by tradition and evolution. In addition, the complete cast of more than 40 officers and numerous battlefields originally featured in the game will be beautifully recreated using Unreal Engine 5, offering peak action and tactical warfare in this thrilling revival. The Dynasty Warriors 3: Xtreme Legends expansion, which is also included, features additional stories for seven officers, including Lu Bu, Meng Huo, and Yuan Shao, as well as bodyguard customization, new weapons, and four types of challenge modes, providing even more gameplay to enjoy in this newly remastered classic. [Koei Tecmo]

games.title: NIPH
games.description: NIPH is a stylish roguelite platformer with risky and intense combat. Slash, shoot, and learn and cast spells with more varied items as you explore a vast and diverse fantasy world!

games.title: Remote Reaper: FPV Drone
games.description: FPV drone simulator. Destroy enemy vehicles with high-precision strikes. Simulation of electronic warfare and realistic armor model.

games.title: Blessing In The Darkness
games.description: A dark fantasy tactical dungeon crawler with an unique turn-based combat system, immersed in a dungeon scroller perspective with dark elements. Featuring minimalist combat and no maps—just pure resource and position management. Go ahead, try to survive, and cross brutal mechanical puzzle pathways!

games.title: Thanks, Light.
games.description: A first-person puzzle game where light turns flat shapes into solid objects. Absorb it to make them flat again. Solve spatial puzzles in a strange world built to be perfect.

games.title: Where It Happened
games.description: You wake up to find yourself standing before an old house. The painful memories buried deep within your heart suddenly return. You don’t remember it well, but you used to live here. This is where it happened.

games.title: The Witch's Bakery
games.description:
The Witch's Bakery is a cozy Adventure RPG about a joyful witch who opens her bakery in modern Paris. She has one special power: she can see into people's heart and heal emotions through magic!

The story progresses through the days as you earn experience, money, and fame, meet new friends and heal their heart.

For some people, their emotion is locked away so strongly than Lunne needs to go inside their heart to help them. She enters their "Heart Palace", a magical space where emotions and thoughts take shape. Lunne needs to guide the personified Emotion back to the heart.

Inside the Heart Palace, Lunne discovers the person's deepest struggles and finds the key ingredient she needs to make a bread that will heal them!

games.title: Thank You Bus Driver
games.description:
Take on the role of a town’s rules-driven (and reckless) bus driver in Thank You Bus Driver! 

Drive fast, slap faster, and toss any rulebreakers out of your bus to reach true victory: being appreciated.

Run a strict bus and you may very well become the best bus driver this town has ever seen.

games.title: SHOCKWAVE TRIGGERS
games.description:
Shockwave Triggers is a vertical scrolling shoot’em up where you’ll choose between 2 pilots – the fast and versatile Amira, whose crystal-sensitive sister has been kidnapped, and the slower but more powerful Turbo B, a mechanic determined to take down the supreme leader of the WW army!

Enjoy anime-style cutscenes and a pumping soundtrack as you blast through 6 unique stages of bullet hell mayhem. Collect crystals from destroyed enemies, initiate shockwaves to cancel incoming projectiles into gems, deploy super attacks and upgrade your ship with character-specific armaments!

Use the shop system to earn new features or buy extra credits, choose from multiple difficulties to suit your playstyle, fill your gallery with unlockable art and use the jukebox feature to enjoy the game’s original soundtrack. Team up for local co-op play, dare to challenge Boss Rush mode and test your skills against online leaderboards!

games.title: ROLLA
games.description: BREAKING NEWS! Downtown is being terrorised by a rolling mass of pulsing flesh! Eyewitnesses describe the scene as “crunchy arcade destruction where survival blends with score-chasing!”. What is this creature!? What are its motives!? Is it really the villain here!? Back to you in the studio.

games.title: Hungry Horrors
games.description: Hungry Horrors is a roguelite deck-building adventure where cooking is your weapon of choice against mythical monsters from British and Irish folklore. Prepare and serve authentic regional dishes to appease these creatures and progress through a world where culinary skills can mean the difference between survival and an unexpected end.

games.title: Deep Dish Dungeon
games.description:
Deep Dish Dungeon is a dungeon crawler and exploration game that rewards curiosity and resourcefulness. In an atmospheric environment, explore corridors, rooms and passageways solo or with up to two friends, and gather resources to improve your camping site. Craft tools and cook nourishing meals to bolster strength throughout the journey, and unravel the enigma that lies within the shadows.

Forage and scavenge as you traverse through the dungeon's bountiful depths. Between your journeys, return to camp and plan your next steps by the fire. Use the resources you find to craft new tools and cook a hearty meal. Remember that food is progress: over time, unlock recipes that have different effects on your stats.

Fortune favors the bold. Take your time to investigate every shadow, solve every puzzle, and open every door. The dungeon will reveal its secrets only if you are patient and persistent. Learn how to defeat enemies with diverse behaviors, discover coveted treasures, and never take a hint for granted.

games.title: Just Dance: Decades of Hits
games.description:
IMMERSIVE EXPERIENCE SPANNING 6 DECADES
Each decade features its own visual identity and carefully curated tracklist, letting you jump between musical eras or build the ultimate throwback-to-modern playlist in one seamless experience. Discover it all through the all-new Adventure Mode, a cheerful story-driven journey that has you dancing your way through the decades.

DANCE TO SONGS EVERYONE KNOWS
Celebrate iconic intergenerational hits brought to life with unique choreography, including fan-favorites like:

- "NUEVAYoL" by Bad Bunny
- "Manchild" by Sabrina Carpenter
- "Danza Kuduro" by Lucenzo & Don Omar
- "Turn Down for What" by DJ Snake & Lil Jon
- "Feel Good Inc." by Gorillaz
- "Bye Bye Bye" by *NSYNC
- "Wannabe" by Spice Girls
- "No Scrubs" by TLC
- "It's Tricky" by Run DMC
- "Uptown Girl" by Billy Joel
- "Mamma Mia" by ABBA

games.title: Battleplan
games.description: Battleplan is a historical, WW2 real-time strategy game of unparalleled realism and simulation. Fight across massive battlefields created from real-world geographic data. Create your army by customizing your order of battle and chain of command. Draw directly on the map to create elaborate plans.

games.title: Alpha Nomos
games.description:
It's time to wield the beat in Alpha Nomos, a rhythm-action roguelite where every instrument is a weapon and every fight moves to the music. Play as Cello and slice through an army of rogue puppets in a vibrant, melody-twisted world where combat pulses to the soundtrack and timing is everything.

Who knew saving the world could sound this good? Join Cello and her friends as they explore their ruined world, fight murderous puppets, and uncover the mysteries of the powerful force known as music. What caused the destruction of this world? What is music? What is Alpha Nomos? All these answers await Cello as she fights to bring balance back to a corrupted world.

Time your moves to the beat to unleash show-stopping combos and perfectly choreographed chaos. Master the rhythm, gather living sound, and breathe life back into a world that moves to the music you make. Prepare for a run where every strike, every upgrade, and every note pulls you deeper into the song.

games.title: Colorbound
games.description: In Colorbound, color is more than just hue. As Anku, an Aymara boy with a unique gift, you’ll harness the power of color to shape the environment itself, uncovering hidden paths to navigate challenging and complex puzzles.

games.title: Burn With Me
games.description: Burn With Me is a story-centric deckbuilder filled with cozy dread and occultic mysteries. In order to summon a Personal Demon you'll master inventive gameplay with position-based synergies, and permanently burn your cards and your soul.

games.title: Time To Wake Up
games.description: You're stuck in a dream. Blink and change your surroundings to escape the shadows of your past.

games.title: Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Expansion
games.description:
Dragon's Dogma 2 presented players with a deep, explorable fantasy world, challenging them to choose their own experience – from the appearance of their Arisen, their vocation, their party, how to approach different situations and more.

With Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen, that experience has been further enhanced through the addition of unforgettable new tales and thrilling encounters.

Experience enhanced gameplay.
Embark on uncharted adventures.
Enticing value for myriad additions.

Together with your loyal Pawns, set off on an unparalleled adventure!

games.title: Hack n' Stack
games.description:
Physics meets tower defense in this chaotic party game.

Craft barricades and turrets with whatever you can find. But beware: relentless waves of enemies are coming to tear down everything you build.

games.title: Sesame Street: Friends & Fun
games.description:
Welcome to Sesame Street! A place to play, laugh and grow.

From the moment you arrive, there’s so much to do. Join Elmo, Tango and the rest of your Sesame Street friends around the neighbourhood!

Walk around with Grover, plant a magical giant beanstalk in Abby’s Garden, find useful tools and rubber ducks in the Community Garden with Bert & Ernie, and work on your number and puzzle skills in Count von Count’s Mansion. Or cook, mix and laugh along with Cookie Monster in his Foodie Truck! Some quests may take a few tries, but you’ll work together to find a way to make the streets a brighter and happier place for everyone.

Make yourself at home! Decorate your house, unlock new mini-games, access exciting new areas of the Street, or throw and unforgettable block party. Spend time with Tango, your cheerful and furry helper or enjoy the whole adventure together with family and friends in local co-op play.

The fun and exploration never ends on Sesame Street!

JOIN THE NEIGHBORHOOD: Create your own character and join Elmo, Tango, Abby and their friends on Sesame Street.

EXPLORE THE STREET: Start at your apartment, stop by Big Bird’s cozy nest, play at the Count’s Mansion, and unlock more places.

BRING EVERYONE TOGETHER: Help the community by going on cooking, photography, and even farming quests solo or in co-op.

DISCOVER AND GROW: Use rewards to decorate your home, unlock new mini-games and access exciting new areas.

TRAVEL WITH TANGO: Take care of Tango just like she’ll take care of you as she helps you get around.

games.title: Whisker Mess
games.description:
Get ready for a feline adventure filled with adorable pieces, clever combinations, and toys scattered everywhere in Whisker Mess! In this fun tile-fitting puzzle, you must place cat-shaped pieces across the board, create lines, and clear the way while earning points and making room for new moves.

By completing horizontal, vertical, and, on certain levels, even diagonal lines, you clear pieces, remove toys from the board, and turn every move into a new strategic opportunity. But be careful: blockers act as extensions of the walls and can completely change the way lines are formed!

With 30 levels divided into 3 biomes, Whisker Mess gradually introduces new challenges. As you progress, you'll encounter special toys with different behaviors, requiring you to carefully observe the board, adapt your plans, and discover how to make the most of each effect.

With no time pressure, Whisker Mess offers a relaxing and accessible experience, while still providing plenty of possibilities for those who enjoy thinking several moves ahead. With different board layouts, varied blockers, and combinations of special toys, each level brings a new challenge to test your creativity and spatial reasoning.

Fit the pieces, create lines, clear the mess, and help turn this feline chaos into pure fun!

games.title: Hood Warfare 2
games.description: Rival gangs fight for control of Chicago. Pick a side, customize your weapons, and fight other players across a variety of action-packed game modes. Spin the block and take over the streets in this chaotic multiplayer FPS.

games.title: Wild Rose: Broken Compass
games.description:
Set sail into a world of adventure, danger, and discovery.

Set sail on a dangerous journey where survival depends on your courage, skill, and ability to adapt.
Explore mysterious islands, discover hidden locations, gather valuable resources, and uncover the secrets scattered across a vast world.
Build your own shelter, craft useful equipment, upgrade your gear, and prepare for the dangers that await beyond the horizon. Fight hostile creatures and enemies, search for treasure, and improve your abilities as you venture deeper into unknown territory.
Every journey is different. Explore at your own pace, decide where to go next, and build your own path to survival.
Explore. Build. Craft. Fight. Survive.
The compass is broken. The journey is yours.

games.title: Hidden Dogs
games.description:
ワンちゃんたちの村へようこそ！ ラビーが極秘ミッションのために、あなたの助けを求めている。そのミッションとは……ワンちゃんたちのビデオゲームを作ること！（ネコちゃんたちは残念ながら、今回は出番がないの）。

イギリスの田園地帯を舞台にした、手描き風の15のステージ。そこに散らばって隠れている500匹以上のワンちゃんたちやアイテムを探し出そう。行き詰まったら、犬笛を吹いてみて！子犬たちを見つけ出すたびに地図は広がり、飛行機やボート、電車なども登場するよ！

ゲームの特徴：
- 500匹以上の犬とアイテムを探し出そう
- 丁寧に描かれた15のステージ
- それぞれに悩みを抱えた4匹のワンちゃんたちの物語
- オリジナルサウンドトラック

reviews.quote: Just Dance: Decades of Hits is a wonderfully entertaining game, and the only thing more fun than playing it is watching someone else dance

A Just Dance that changes its name more than its formula. While the new Adventure Mode adds little to the experience, the game is still the perfect excuse to get everyone off the couch and onto the dance floor.

Just Dance: Decades of Hits works where it matters. At the end of the day it’s a fun workout game that allows for a lot of flexibility when it comes to the song choice. It has an annoying but ultimately unobtrusive way of asking you to spend more money, but if you find the main game is worth it, who's to say the extras aren’t worth it to you, too?

Battleplan is the first game that makes me feel like I was playing RISK as a kid with adults who knew much better than me. Generally speaking, strategy games either give you full tactical control or go grand and make you handle taxation on wood imports from your neighbor. Battleplan strikes a balance by giving you an intimate view of the action but from the general's chair. The realistic depiction of historical engagements is a treat, with mechanics that never go deeper than they have to in order to deliver unforgettable emergent narratives. As it is, Battleplan is a great game, and some quality-of-life additions to the interface are all that's left from making it the perfect strategy title.

Battleplan does something intriguing by mixing a highly detailed real-time strategy experience based on World War II with relatively limited player control over the action. Planning via drawing is accessible and fast, and the game encourages players to try out strategies and replay battles. The OOB and officer upgrade system is very good. The presentation is decent, although zooming in to see how units actually do battle isn’t advised, and there’s plenty of attention to detail in the battle setup and briefings. Battleplan is a good game for anyone who feels intimidated by the complexity of most military strategy but might be too hands-off for some hardcore genre fans.

Alpha Nomos can be a little repetitive at times, and it can feel as though there isn’t an abundance of content to unlock, but it still remains a fairly fun and distinctly creative experience throughout. The game’s unique mix of rhythm-game mechanics and roguelike progression, paired with its fun story and characters, makes for an undeniably memorable experience.

Colorbound is a small yet great and colourful journey all about life and its inevitable end. With a gripping soundtrack, tricky puzzles, and just seeing the sheer amount of love on display, this is highly recommended.
Burn With Me is a dreadfully cosy little game where forethought and planning will get you through with sanity intact.

Just like protagonist Alan alternates between two versions of his mind's reality, Time To Wake Up alternates between being an underwhelming and a brilliant one. While the Belgian Eye Blink Twice holds two very interesting cards - being an important story regarding depression and an clever core mechanic of blinking to swap the scenery - it doesn't seem to feel comfortable playing any of them with conviction throughout the full two hours. There's something beautiful to be found in Time To Wake Up, but it takes a couple of blinks to really see it.

This new collection cements the Nintendo Switch 2’s reputation as a great console for third-party ports, with a impressive array of games that look and run spectacularly even in handheld mode, particularly the most visually stunning of them all, Kingdom Hearts III.

Overall, Kingdom Hearts Collection 1-3 on Switch 2 is a fantastic package that is so close to being completely on par with the Integrum Masterpiece release. Kingdom Hearts 3 and A Fragmentary Passage’s framerate issues are the only things stopping it from definitively being my new favourite way to play, but the ability to go portable is worth those minor issues. Whether you’re a complete newcomer preparing for Kingdom Hearts 4 or a diehard fan like me looking for an excuse to replay, Kingdom Hearts Collection 1-3 on Switch 2 is a fantastic way to do it.

KINGDOM HEARTS Collection [I~III] is an ambitious, emotionally resonant package that highlights the series’ remarkable highs, messy experiments, and constant reinvention. Its native Switch 2 release finally fixes one of the franchise’s biggest accessibility problems, while Critical Mode, Re Mind, and years of updates make Kingdom Hearts III far stronger than it was at launch. However, uneven world design, inconsistent combat systems across entries, performance hiccups on Switch 2, and the continued absence of playable 358/2 Days, Re:coded, Melody of Memory, and the full χ saga prevent this from feeling truly definitive.

Kingdom Hearts Collection [I~III] is an excellent way to experience most of the Kingdom Hearts franchise, whether for the first time or for the umpteenth. Most of the bundled games deliver essentially perfect performance on the Nintendo Switch 2, while the more recent games still maintain consistent enough frame rates to please most. Being able to play the entire franchise on the go is a thrilling prospect, and I’ll likely be doing so for a good long while to come. This is a great way to get ready for Kingdom Hearts IV, and I’m sure many Nintendo-exclusive fans will be doing just that with this top-notch bundle.

Kingdom Hearts Collection [I～III] is an incredible package that brings nearly the entire saga together in one place. I would have liked to see a performance and frame rate toggle for Kingdom Hearts III, and the $75 asking price is a little steep considering how cheap this collection is on other platforms. At the end of the day, though, it’s Kingdom Hearts finally on Switch 2, and it’s hard to ask for much more.
KINGDOM HEARTS Collection (I-III) gives owners of the Nintendo Switch 2 a fantastic collection of games that all run superbly on the hardware. It is finally here!

Kingdom Hearts Collection [I–III] is the definitive collection of the series, offering everything fans need to know to prepare for the fourth numbered entry. A highlight is the Switch 2 version, which finally allows console owners to run the games natively and with good performance.

The Kingdom Hearts Collection [1~3] is the definitive way to experience the saga, offering polished ports and nearly the entire lore on Nintendo Switch 2. Despite minor performance dips, it’s the best entry point for newcomers and a nostalgic return for veterans.

Gears of War: E-Day is, for me, the best game in the series and The Coalition's finest work to date. Its campaign brings Marcus and Dom back without relying solely on nostalgia, delivering a darker and more brutal take on the origins of the Locust threat.

Gears of War: E-Day is a monumental triumph from a developer that irrefutably understands what’s important to fans: Gears isn’t just about tearing through Locust with a chainsaw, it’s about brotherhood, sacrifice, and grief. The Coalition has delivered an unforgettable campaign packed full of fresh ideas whilst staying true to what makes Gears so special. The Locust are back and more terrifying than ever, and blasting them to bits is incredibly satisfying. This is the best the combat has felt in twenty years, and fighting to survive the fall of Kalona will leave you speechless. Through its stunning locations, characters, and cinematics, E-Day is a visual powerhouse and one of the best-looking games I’ve ever seen on Xbox.

Weapons of all kinds, gadgets, and locations brimming with possibilities form the foundation of a story that excels in every aspect. Marcus and Dom return alongside old and new acquaintances in a prequel that feels fresh and invigorating. The story of Kalona’s downfall on E-Day serves as the starting point for a war-torn odyssey filled with unique situations, memorable scenes, and the feeling of experiencing an iconic moment in a saga that, for many, is a must-play. Gears of War: E-Day marks a turning point for the Xbox catalog with a console and PC exclusive that’s determined to raise the bar for Microsoft.
A campaign executed to perfection in terms of both technical aspects and gameplay. A brutal and intense war spectacle featuring the best Gears story to date.

I have to say that Gears of War: E-Day is an absolute triumph of a game. The maps in the multiplayer and the campaign are big, with things to find in unlikely corners. From there, exploration in the story mode should be seen as its own reward. This is a game full of content, and you’ll spend hours upon hours taking in everything it has to offer.  Whether you’re here for the campaign, or prefer to get invested in the multiplayer, if you have the slightest interest in Gears, you have to play Gears of War: E-Day. It really is that simple.

Gears of War: E-Day delivers arguably the franchise's finest, most atmospheric campaign, brilliantly balancing pulse-pounding action with genuine horror roots. By pairing breathtaking Series X visuals and refined combat with a deeply emotional return to Marcus and Dom, The Coalition has delivered a masterclass prequel that restores complete faith in Xbox's future. A triumph from start to finish.

Gears of War: E-Day shines by showing off humanity's perseverance. Every new character stands out, never overshadowed by the legacy of Marcus or Dom. Even with the game taking place in one city over several days, the evolution of that city and its inhabitants has created fleshed-out characters that you're rooting for the success of every step of the way.

E-Day succeeds in telling the story of Emergence Day in a gripping, desperate, and most importantly, fun way. The culmination of 20 years as a franchise, refining everything the series is into a must-play XBOX title that takes you on a gloriously brutal, emotionally-satisfying, and epic, cinematic adventure.

Gears of War: E-Day delivers arguably the series’ strongest campaign, combining mature, restrained storytelling with the return of Marcus Fenix’s charismatic presence. Already among the franchise’s finest entries, it could become a serious Game of the Year contender if its content-rich multiplayer matches the campaign’s quality. I thought Lucas would be a character who gives us an outlook of E-Day through someone who’s never seen the horrors of the pendulum wars and war in general. At first it seemed to be going that way in Act 1 but went NO WHERE after that. He was desensitized to it all immediately and just asked basic questions here and there. A scene in act 4 also took a lot of seriousness out. We come to learn Lucas broke strict protocol and mentions how he wanted to experience being on the front lines of the Pendulum wars with his friends, so he decided to hold a prolonged communication with his old friends as they were fighting the UIR. Turns out the indies tracked the signal and they all died because of him. At first, you see how that experience really broke him. Understandable. But what utterly destroyed this scene was Mags coming in saying how “we all get it wrong.” SERIOUSLY LOL? Get it wrong lol? Writing like this just never felt like the game could be taken seriously. In act 3 Marcus tells Mags who he’s barely known for 2 days about the truth behind Carlos LMAO. 

The final fight was very average feeling like a modernized version of RAAMs fight in Gears 1, and the story overall felt rushed towards the end and didn’t really land. The open sections and acts 2-4 were also very bare bones. They were very detailed and looked stunning, but had no substance in them. The over abundance of hard cases all over these maps was very frustrating to grab and I don’t understand how anyone can find all of them without looking at a guide.

Overall, I feel like this game is best to play using gamepass or grab on sale. I cannot believe they charged $100 for a FOMO edition. Let alone the base $70 price tag. I do believe this game can be a solid foundation for what comes next as they’ve already built out a lot of what they would need for future installments. That is if the studio gets another shot after this. The Gears franchise has been in a niche corner for a LONG time. And with the creative decisions they’re making some good but still a lot more bad I don’t know who this franchise is for anymore. Newer audiences have no interest in Gears of War. And we can see that with data on the last three games. And the core audience seems to be fading as well. At this point just remake Gears 2 and let the franchise rest

For me, Star Wars: Galactic Racer has become the perfect arcade racing game experience that leaves nothing to be desired. The sense of speed is the best it’s been since the first WipeOut, and it not only looks stunning, but sounds and plays that way, too. Star Wars: Galactic Racer is not only one of the best racing games I have played all year, but after playing the campaign the full way through, it just might be one of my favourite racing games of all time.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer absolutely nails what it is trying to do. It is a high-octane racer that's endless fun to play, and it looks fantastic. This would have been a great game with a standard single-player mode, but what is here is inventive and engaging. I'd have loved a few silly classic characters and another planet or two, but this is a game I'll return to for a long time.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is everything I hoped it would be. Fuse built a campaign that keeps giving me reasons to master the tracks, then made the racing feel good enough that I wanted to.  And for my fellow Episode I Racer lovers: Galactic Racer’s marketing has kept the podracers in the background, but don’t let that fool you. By the time I was done with the campaign, I found myself happy and whispering one thing to myself: Now this is podracing.

These worlds don't just look beautiful, from Jakku's dunes and wrecked Star Destroyers you must thread between to Crait's white crystalline surface with red dust billowing underneath. They're also carved up into fascinating tracks that blend tight underground corridors where cornering is a constant discussion with death, and daringly wide-open outside sections where I once got so turned around I ended up going backwards. These are places that constantly shift in the way that they challenge you, and I suspect that better racers than me will spend an awfully long time working out the optimal strategies for handling each one.

Star Wars Galactic Racer is a Star-Wars-authentic thrill rush that may be the best racer in a decade. It’s such a wonderful, engaging experience that literally does everything right. Just be warned – as a roguelite – the on-ramp can take time while presenting a higher difficulty level.

While the lack of local multiplayer is unfortunate, the decision to drop the mode so that the game is kept at a locked frame-rate is the right one. The game is so fast-paced that you need every millisecond possible. The tracks are all excellent, the music and sound effects are jaw-dropping, and both gameplay and customization have a ton of depth. The single player campaign is surprisingly good and has a lot more under the hood than I was expecting. Its roguelike elements are well-thought out, and will keep you coming back for more well after you beat the game. Online multiplayer has a variety of modes, from traditional arcade style races to entire tours across the galaxy, so that every type of player can find something to enjoy. Overall, Star Wars: Galactic Racer has just the right amount of nostalgia, and is a true evolution of the podracing experience. It’s frenetic, bombastic, and above all else, incredibly fun.

Star Wars Galactic Racer is a spectacular surprise and a must-play for racing and Star Wars fans. It shines with exhilarating speed, excellent online support, a smart build system, and a fantastic dose of Podracing nostalgia. While its roguelite structure may not appeal to those looking for a traditional campaign, the quality of its racing and combat makes it one of the best Star Wars games in recent years.

Fuse Games have truly given Millennial gamers like myself that spiritual successor to Star Wars Episode I: Racer that we never got. And to them, I give them all the grace that a post-Empire galaxy allows us.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a spectacular and surprisingly thrilling racing game that delivers an excellent Star Wars experience through its run-based gameplay, strategic choices, and spectacular crashes.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve exemplifies “High-Flying Action” and takes it to another level, while also giving new fans options to ease into it. Personally, I say dive into the deep end; flying directly into the ground a few times puts some hair on your chest. If you enjoy exploring an action game in a massive 3D space, love jets and airplanes, or are already a fan of the franchise, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a masterclass in its category.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a bold evolution of the foundation laid in AC7. Its story is more exciting, its presentation is more polished, and most importantly, its gameplay is impeccable, with a variety of missions and combat situations that keep the player engaged, entertained, and wanting more. This is one of the best games not only of the year, but of the generation.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve elevates the franchise to new heights with a spectacular campaign that mixes high octane missions with relevant thematic storytelling. The real ace, though, remains the compelling and addictive dogfighting gameplay.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is an improvement in everything that is quintessentially “Ace Combat," bringing back squadron commands and adding a plethora of different aircraft, new special weapons, and more. The cinematic visuals and deep, twisting narrative immerse the player in the fantasy of being an ace pilot in a war between two nations.
Ace Combat 8 is a love letter to combat aviation in its entirety. It showcases aircraft as bringers of both death and salvation, but from an earnest, human perspective.

Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is a spectacular return for the long-running flight combat series, combining exceptionally responsive controls with stunning audiovisual presentation and a substantial 30-mission campaign. Its blend of accessible arcade action and deeper simulation elements makes every dogfight satisfying, while an engaging story, extensive aircraft customization, and multiplayer provide plenty of longevity. Upgrades can feel unnecessary on standard difficulty, but this is otherwise an impressively complete package and one of the strongest flight combat games of the modern era.
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve gives you total freedom in how you fly and fight, with plenty of customisation options and visuals that'll blow you away.

The years roll by—now counted in decades given the series' longevity—yet it is delightful to see Ace Combat endure as a franchise crafted with passion and love for both video games and its loyal fanbase. Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve stands as one of the franchise's finest entries, undoubtedly earning a spot in the conversation for the series' greatest title of all time. From the very start, it is a beautiful, fun, and challenging game that captures the true essence of gaming through its focus on design and mechanics. Project Aces—now Bandai Namco Aces—remains true to its vision without compromising its identity. Without a doubt, this is one of the year's best games and an experience not to be missed.

After 30 years of soaring to new heights, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve finally reaches the summit and stands undisputed. Refined in every possible way, it is not only the finest game in the series to date, but arguably one of the greatest air combat simulations ever made.

ACE Combat 8: Wings of the Theve from Bandai Namco Aces Inc. is a marvelous, beautiful dogfighting flight simulator. It offers a solid storyline with real stakes, a good variety of missions to keep the game engaging and fun, and accessible gameplay that should satisfy both newbies and veterans of the series.

I have been in the skies of Strangereal since Air Combat on the original PlayStation. I have completed every entry in the franchise. After 145 hours with Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, including achieving Platinum with the ultra rare Ace of Aces trophy requiring S rank on every mission at ACE difficulty, I can say without hesitation that Wings of Theve is the best Ace Combat game ever made. It surpasses Ace Combat 5: The Unsung War, which held that title for over two decades in my personal ranking.

Storyline

Project Aces has consistently delivered narratives that punch above the weight of what an aerial combat game should be capable of producing. Wings of Theve continues that tradition at the highest level the series has ever reached. The story respects franchise lore, advances the Strangereal timeline in a direction that has longtime fans watching the approach toward Ace Combat 3 Electrosphere territory with genuine excitement, and delivers emotional beats that land because the character work earns them. For players new to the series, it functions as a compelling standalone entry. For veterans who have followed Strangereal for decades, it rewards that investment meaningfully.

Gameplay

The moment to moment aerial combat is the most refined the series has delivered. The new control scheme is accessible for new players entering the franchise and represents a genuine design consideration for that audience. Veteran players who prefer the classic framework have Type B available and I returned to it immediately. Both work. The choice existing is the right decision.
The ACE difficulty S rank requirement is exactly what the series needed. This is not a participation trophy challenge. Clearing every mission including free missions at ACE with S rank demands genuine mechanical mastery of the aircraft, weapon systems, and mission design. The Ace of Aces trophy sitting at 0.3% rarity at time of writing reflects exactly how demanding that requirement is. It is the kind of challenge that justifies extended time investment and delivers genuine satisfaction when completed.

Music

Everflow and Hortus Regis Alti belong in the conversation for best tracks in the franchise's history, and Ace Combat's musical history is exceptional. The soundtrack as a whole is phenomenal and serves both the combat sequences and the narrative moments with the tonal precision the series has always delivered.

Technical Performance

Reviewed on base PS5, LG OLED G3 in Game Optimizer HGiG mode, and Samsung HW-Q990D in Game Mode Pro. The game performs beautifully on base hardware. The PS5 Pro Enhanced version likely elevates this further but the base experience is polished and visually strong throughout.

Content and Longevity

145 hours in and the Campaign Medal completions and online content still remain. The MRP grind for the 25,000,000 total required for trophy purposes alone represents substantial content engagement. The upcoming super aircraft DLCs are something I am genuinely looking forward to, as the franchise tradition of legendary aircraft additions has always extended the experience meaningfully.

For New and Returning Players

Wings of Theve works as both a franchise entry point and a veteran celebration. New players get a complete, compelling aerial combat experience with an accessible control option. Returning players get a love letter to everything that has made Strangereal one of gaming's most underappreciated fictional universes.

The AC3 Question

The timeline is approaching Electrosphere territory. Project Aces, if you are reading reviews: do not remaster. Remake. Ace Combat 3 deserves the full treatment and Wings of Theve has proven the team is capable of delivering it at the highest level.

10/10. The best Ace Combat game ever made. Essential for fans of the series and a genuine recommendation for anyone who has never played one. Get in the cockpit.

For their very first game, Wych Elm have blown it out of the park. I recommend Silver Pines to everyone: fans of horror, Metroidvanias, and detective stories. I even encourage those new to those genres to try it out, as it encapsulates a beautifully cinematic experience with a story you’ll want to uncover for yourself.

Silver Pines is a cerebrally divine love letter to David Lynch and all the narrative trademarks he was known for, from the cult classic Twin Peaks to Blue Velvet and Lost Highway. It digs even deeper to its spiritual successor Silent Hill, from the fog-filled streets to the nightmares that lurk with bared teeth, and embraces all those inspirations with the utmost grace and respect while still very much telling its own story. Combat can take a bit to get used to, but feels satisfying after a while with plenty of options at Walker's disposal. Meanwhile, the core investigation aspect of the game is well-executed if a bit unforgiving to the distracted player.

For their very first attempt, Wych Elm have knocked it out of the park. The influences from the masterworks of Lynch, Remedy and Silent Hill, the thriller steeped in ’90s Americana, the discovery of the city’s secrets, and that sense of unease and anticipation about what we’ll encounter every time we step into a new area, blended together in an unforgettable experience.

Silver Pines is a horror search-action game that borrows concepts from established games in the genre and uses them wonderfully to strengthen its own gameplay. The tanky controls and limited inventory kept me anxious as I tried to survive in this abandoned town, while the slowly unravelling story made me doubt whether Red Walker was as sane as he first seemed. The search for Eddie Velvet is a gaming experience that will haunt you like few other PI investigations can.

Compelling, atmospheric, and brilliant, Silver Pines is a dive into mystery that's hard to put down and even harder to let go. It makes you feel like a detective, an action hero, and a man on the brink of uncovering horrifying darkness all at once.

Silver Pines is a great survival-horror that came just at the perfect time. The story is intriguing, the atmosphere is gloomy and creepy, the puzzles are intricate and interesting, and the combat is decent and enjoyable. The minor missed steps with its story and aiming guns are easily forgiven when looking at the bigger picture, and it’s hard not to love it.

Silver Pines is an atmospheric game, a Metroidvania-style survival horror title that draws heavily from genre classics like Silent Hill, Resident Evil, and Alan Wake, as well as from television and film, such as Twin Peaks, The X-Files, and The Shining. However, these inspirations don’t reduce Wych Elm’s work to a mere collection of references; thanks to excellent storytelling, they allow the game to carve out its own path between nightmare and mystery. Solid gameplay underpins the experience, reinterpreting the genre’s conventions without forcing a radical overhaul. It’s also impossible not to mention the excellent art direction, featuring rotoscoped animations, and the soundtrack, with atmospheric music that heightens the tension. Silver Pines is a haunting adventure, a glimpse into the mystery of identity that straddles the line between reality and imagination.

Silver Pines is a glorious revival of the 90s survival horror formula. Fans of the early Silent Hill and Resident Evil games will be thrilled by a title that perfectly distills those classics' formulas, opting for 2D gameplay with strong Metroidvania elements.

Silver Pines is yet another excellent indie horror game and would not be out of place as part of the Silent Hill franchise. The combination of survival horror and more involved platforming exploration works fantastically well, while the town is chock-full of hidden secrets with enigmatic mysteries to solve.

Silver Pines is a sharp, moody debut. It mixes survival horror and Metroidvania design with real confidence. The hand-drawn art is gorgeous. All in all, the atmosphere is thick and unsettling. The mystery pulls you forward, and the world rewards curiosity. Combat feels stiff and lacks satisfaction. The game commits to old-school design. If you love atmospheric horror and don’t mind a slow burn, Silver Pines is a must-play this Halloween season.

Planet Zoo 2 raises the bar for the simulation genre, with new features and quality-of-life tweaks making the latest Frontier Developments title not only as the kings of the jungle, but also conquerors of the sea and the air.
Most importantly, every creature feels well-designed and well-thought-out. They don’t behave the same, and I lost so many hours simply observing what my favorite inhabitants were up to.

With lovely visual upgrades to its sprawling roster of land, air, and sea-dwelling animals and exciting expanded mechanics, Planet Zoo 2 is a vibrant and thriving sequel. I wasn't absolutely awed by all of the new stuff, and in particular I think wildlife reserves could be a lot richer than they are. But with plenty of management features to challenge my strategy-loving side and endlessly flexible building tools to inspire my creative side, there's not a lot more I could ask for. It's a roaring success.
Planet Zoo 2 isn’t a revolution, but it doesn’t need to be. It takes what made the original great and improves upon it in every way.

It's safe to say that Planet Zoo 2 is Frontier's biggest and best game yet. It looks fantastic, has a huge range of animals, and its greater focus on conservation makes for a wholesome and rewarding experience. There's a learning curve involved, though, so be prepared to put in the time if you want to get the most out of this wonderful sim.

Planet Zoo 2 is a stupendous upgrade over Frontier's first effort from 2019. The improvements made to the animal AI pathing, zoo customization and the new habitats areastounding. Frontier has made tremendous strides in this sequel, and while it may feel overwhelming to new players even with its comprehensive story mode, it may be a bit too much all at once in some places. That being said, absolutely nothing should stop you from taking the plunge into this spectacular zoo management simulation.

Planet Zoo 2 is, in my opinion, one of the best management sims ever made. The level of detail in not just the animals, but also the technical details and real-world education provided is like no other. It's so easy to lose yourself in a zoo, creating the perfect habitats for the amazing animals and truly feeling responsible for them and their well-being. The addition of aviaries and aquariums is a welcome one, and it's incredibly enjoyable to have the option to turn off the UI, go into a cinematic mode and simply watch the animals do their thing.
The fantastic aquariums and aviaries make Planet Zoo 2 the ultimate zoo simulator, though quite a few animals from multiple continents are still needed to make that dream complete.

Planet Zoo 2 is an engaging and rewarding management sim with gorgeous animal models and animations, alongside remarkable creative freedom. Despite a few shortcomings, some of which it has inherited from its predecessor, it is an excellent choice for players who love detailed management, though those primarily seeking a relaxing experience with animals may find it overwhelming.

What surprised me most about Allogloom is how much it reminded me of the point-and-click games I played when I was younger, without ever feeling childish. A straight line runs from the curiosity that made me click everything in Putt-Putt, Pajama Sam, or Freddi Fish to the curiosity that kept pulling me deeper into Gruesome Grove and the world around it. The difference is what waits on the other side of the click. Those childhood games rewarded curiosity with jokes, animations, and friendly characters; Allogloom sometimes rewards it with something you probably wish you didn’t know, and I mean that as a compliment. Perhaps that’s why the comparison to those childhood adventures feels so correct. Allogloom feels like the genre grew up alongside the people who played them. The curiosity is still there, as are the strange characters and the inventory full of seemingly useless nonsense, but the questions are different now, and the answers can be considerably more uncomfortable. It reminded me why I used to click on absolutely everything in Putt-Putt, Pajama Sam, and Freddi Fish, without ever wanting to replay any of those games. We’re older now, and the moths grew up with us. Allogloom is definitely one of those point-and-click games I’ll recommend for years to come.
Allogloom is a beautiful, short game with an amazing, twisted art style, deep lore, and simple yet fun puzzles.

For those who want a neatly packaged, slightly eerie, yet beautiful escape to another world, Allogloom is amazing. If anything, I wish I could’ve had just a little bit more about the spaces we visit to see what was happening in each area. Again, this isn’t anything that’s a true negative, but I did end up with just a few questions on some of the areas we find ourselves. I want to learn more about the settings that have been created for Nora. The areas she finds herself in all seem to have their own reasons for being and I’d want just a little more to understand why. But even without this, Allogloom is a game worth your time if you want a bit of horror with your point and click games.
A macabre take on other worlds and how one perceives reality, Allogloom is a creepy-cute point-and-click treat for fans of haunting tales.

In its logic strings, Aloogloom is so satisfying. There’s victory in discovering exactly which item works with another, and that’s what all good point-and-click adventures should aspire to achieve. Pair this system with Allogloom‘s lush, moody artwork and its layered, macabre themes, and it’s an entirely unique experience that is rich and beautiful in approach. It’s a very strong debut from developer Galactic Ghosty, and one that deserves your attention.

Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition is an accessible and modern experience that draws new players into the struggle to unify Japan for the first time, while allowing longtime fans to rediscover this beloved game. Those approaching Creative Assembly’s title for the first time can experience that entire historical period from start to finish, from the rise of the samurai to their fall, thanks to the inclusion of the Rise of the Samurai and Fall of the Samurai expansions. Veterans, on the other hand, will find a game with restored graphics and many quality-of-life improvements to the gameplay. Total War: Shogun 2 remains a masterpiece of the strategy genre to this day, and this new Complete Edition gives us yet another excuse to fight for the shogunate.

It's a spectacular, enormous experience that strategy fans will undoubtedly be happy to play for hundreds of hours, and it should serve as the definitive introduction to the series for new fans moving forward. Is it the best Total War game of all time? Though I definitely have a soft spot for the original Rome release, it's fair to say that this is just about as good as it gets in the genre.

The new edition corrects high-resolution interface issues, modernizes controls, adds the option to adjust settings in the Divided Kingdom, and includes important current graphical features. Total War: SHOGUN 2 - Complete Edition makes it easy to return to one of the best campaigns in the series.

Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition crafts a deep experience. It serves its grand strategy far better than its RTS combat, making enjoyment depend on which side of the gameplay you are mostly looking forward to.

Total War: Shogun 2 Complete Edition is something I’m absolutely thrilled to have in my life. I looked at it with rose-coloured sake glasses, and it did not disappoint. This is every bit the experience I recall from half a lifetime ago, with a new coat of ukiyo-e paint. The new visuals are absolutely stunning and bring one of the Total War franchise’s quintessential titles into modernity. I like to think I am a master of the new tactical features, but I fear that is far from the truth. This is a great “Complete Edition” for fans and newcomers alike.

I’m left feeling thoroughly satisfied with this grand new addition to a game I already loved. Dark Arisen has not only made Dragon’s Dogma 2 a must-play RPG, but it’s also one of Capcom’s best games in years.

Returning to Dragon's Dogma II is a treat in itself, but tack on a couple dozen hours of fantastic new content in a harsh but beautiful new region, and this is the best the game has ever been. Dark Arisen's unique loot cycle and challenging encounters work alongside a compelling new story to make it worth every penny.

If you love the idea of a grand fantasy adventure and experience a truly unique and immersive single-player game where you feel as if you’re actually accompanied by real players going on treacherous adventures together, with great moment-to-moment gameplay, then please, please play Dragon’s Dogma 2, then continue your adventure into Dark Arisen DLC and the cold lands of Norgan.

Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is often Capcom's open world RPG at its absolute peak. It's one hell of a meaty expansion, delivering a surprisingly involved story, joyous exploration, and deeply compelling combat. A transformative DLC.

Whether you’re a lapsed Arisen returning to the world of Dragon’s Dogma or a curious newcomer finally taking the plunge after Capcom’s stellar track record convinced you it was worth it, Dark Arisen proves to be an absolute delight. It builds upon the excellent foundation Capcom’s been polishing for the past two years, with sharp combat and engaging exploration. It challenges you with brutal new trials, all the while making the grind less unbearable. It cements Dragon’s Dogma 2 as an unforgettable experience.

Dragon’s Dogma II: Dark Arisen does what the original expansion had accomplished and set the bar with 20 hours more. With both Dark Arisen’s original premise and the Lost Rites challenges, there is more things to do, fight, and see, within the world even before deciding to end it at the finishing fight. While some things do remain the same from its 2024 base, the effort and vastness make up for it doesn’t demand a slow crawl, but a satisfying slow pain-and-gain run. For those who could tear themselves away from Crimson Desert, this Action RPG might be for you.

The Dark Arisen expansion for Dragon’s Dogma 2 adds a ton of new content to the base game, along with much-needed quality-of-life improvements that make the overall experience the most definitive one yet. If you enjoyed the base game, Dark Arisen is a must-play.

Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is an excellent expansion that builds on the base game's strongest elements while ironing out enough of the friction its weaker parts caused upon release. It advances the foundations of its exploration and combat loop, making it feel like the definitive version of those systems and something worth diving into right away.

Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is what expansions are truly about. The wholly distinct and dangerous region of Norgan sends players to explore the treacherous cold for new threats. What will be uncovered is a rich story, phenomenal encounters, and a wealth of new content that pushes Dragon’s Dogma 2 into the territory of an unforgettable journey.

Order of the Sinking Star is a masterpiece. Its immaculate, mind-bending puzzles are perfectly designed to make you feel spectacularly stupid and then phenomenally smart. Its interconnected world, progressive revelation of layered mechanics, and post-credits continuation make it the ultimate Sokoban experience.

Order of the Sinking Star is a demanding and inventive puzzle adventure that constantly finds new ways to challenge your understanding of its rules. Its four distinct worlds, character-driven limitations, and increasingly intertwined mechanics make solving puzzles deeply satisfying, even if prolonged roadblocks can sometimes become exhausting.

Even after The Witness, Braid, and the many PuzzleScript games and Sokoban-likes that form its foundation, I'm sure I've never played anything to match. It’s not just a game of the year contender; fall in its clutches, Order of the Sinking Star might also end up the game you simply play the most, even—and most importantly—when you’re far away from the screen.

There’s no doubt that Order of the Sinking Star is one of the best puzzle games out there. The continual evolution of mechanics sprawling across a puzzle-ridden overworld is vast and exciting, and it’s so cool to see it all come from the same core concept. I like that it tells different stories within this, which leads to the bigger mystery of where we are to begin with. Sometimes it can feel a little overwhelming with every new mechanic introduced and then asked to apply, but it can also create some interesting scenarios that are enjoyable to play through.

Order of the Sinking Star is a massive, generous work full of discoveries, capable of reminding us that the best puzzle games aren't about finding a solution, but about learning to see the world in a different way.

Order of the Sinking Star is a massive and often brilliant puzzle game, built around the idea of constantly evolving rules that initially seem to have exhausted their potential. Its best moments come when different mechanics begin to interact, forcing players to rethink what they thought they had already learned. That same ambition can also weigh the experience down. With more than 1,400 puzzles, the sheer amount of content can sometimes feel excessive, while the difficulty occasionally depends more on remembering old rules than on finding an elegant solution. Even so, it remains an exceptional game for anyone looking for a demanding puzzle experience and willing to invest a considerable amount of time.

Order of the Sinking Star hands you more than a thousand handcrafted puzzles and no tutorials, and that trust makes it special. Intuitive character abilities, four distinct worlds, and a shared Overworld give every solution a sense of ownership, while undo and restart keep experimentation painless. The same philosophy backfires when progress stalls with no sign of what you missed, and the scale wears thin over long sessions. For patient problem-solvers, it is an excellent fit.

Order of the Sinking Star demands a lot from its players, but rewards them with plenty of variety through four distinct directions, each with its own mechanics, style and story. The lack of hints and increasing difficulty can be frustrating, especially for casual puzzlers, but the way the different systems come together in the Gold Rooms creates satisfying aha-moments. It is a game that trusts players to think for themselves, making it a rewarding challenge for puzzle enthusiasts.

Order of the Sinking Star is the most unique puzzle game I’ve ever encountered. Seemingly endless innovation and evolution of mechanics are just some of the key aspects of this game. While it doesn’t always hit the mark in terms of story delivery or length, it maintains its unusual gameplay throughout the many hours of gameplay. If you’re a fan of puzzles, then there’s never been a game more made for you.

Order of the Sinking Star might work better had it been a bit more curated in deploying its massive pile of puzzles, but the occasional frustration and overcomplication is an affordable price of admission to play around with so many fun ideas.

Echo Weaver is a thrilling metroidbrainia that turns knowledge into progression, combining a tightly designed time loop with expressive platforming, rewarding exploration, and an engrossing mystery. Its abilities continually recontextualize the world and encourage experimentation, making repeat playthroughs especially compelling. A few minor progression quirks and the strict loop timer may not work for everyone, but Moonlight Kids delivers an inventive and deeply satisfying take on the metroidvania formula.

Echo Weaver is a very compelling concept for a Metroidvania, and presents some truly great gameplay ideas that I don’t think I’ve seen before. It’s a melding of various mechanics and while some of the resulting design choices make the game stumble just short of reaching excellence, the overall experience is one I can still see echoing in my brain for a long time to come.

Echo Weaver successfully blends story and time-manipulation gameplay into a "metroidBRAINia" experience—one where progress stems from the gradual acquisition of knowledge, mechanics, and abilities that were available all along, even if the player didn't realize it. Exploration via time loops is dynamic, and new discoveries are logged in an accessible, instructive way; however, the sheer number of shortcuts, techniques, and connections can eventually become mind-boggling, complicating the flow of this beautiful 2D platformer. The world itself is a massive puzzle, making the game recommended for those who enjoy unraveling the intricacies of its inner workings.

Echo Weaver’s unique approach to the Metroid structure is admirable, unique, and well executed. The sense of discovery is fantastic, and though I realistically probably won’t immediately play the game again, the idea that I could start with knowledge of basically all of the abilities to rip through the game at high speed is an enticing one. Developer Moonlight Kids puts a lot of trust in the player to figure out how it all works, and the reward is palpable. That trust leads to some frustrated, aimless wandering, and the platforming challenges occasionally venture into feeling unfair, but by the end you will feel like a genius. That’s a good feeling to leave a game with.

Echo Weaver is a bold take on the Metroidvania formula: a tightly constructed adventure that wholeheartedly commits to familiar science fiction elements and, in the process, makes them its own. Endlessly creative, sometimes frustrating, but always ingenious, it will worm its way into your brain and won’t let you go until you’re satisfied you’ve done everything it will let you. My advice is to play it today, with a few hours set aside for the first of several sessions that you’ll likely spend before you see and do everything. You’ll probably want them.
